concepts.title: Accelerator memory and peer dataflow
concepts.meaning: Data moves from device memory into local tiles, through compute, and across peer links when needed.
concepts.brief: Trace a working tile from device memory into on-chip local storage, through a compute engine, then over a peer link when the workload requires another device. Mark the owner and capacity boundary at each stage.
pitfalls: Capacity and bandwidth belong to specific memory levels and owners.
Peer exchange may route over a shared link or host staging; measure the actual topology.

headings: Memory paths: capacity belongs to an owner
Interconnect topologies: count exchanges, then measure the route

concepts.title: Collective reduce-scatter ownership
concepts.meaning: Matching tensor chunks reduce across ranks and each rank retains the chunk at its own index.
concepts.brief: Give four ranks four-element vectors. Reduce corresponding indices, move the completed chunks through a ring or tree schedule, and leave chunk r on rank r. Then optionally run all-gather to reconstruct the full vector everywhere. Keep rank order, communicator agreement, buffer offsets and stream completion visible.
pitfalls: Reduce-scatter leaves one reduced shard per rank; it does not leave the full tensor everywhere.
Every rank must call matching collectives in matching order with compatible arguments.
In-place reduce-scatter and all-gather use rank-offset shard locations, not automatically the buffer base.

headings: Choose the operation from desired ownership

concepts.title: GPU compiler artifact ownership
concepts.meaning: Source code is compiled into packaged device images with architecture-specific ownership and target rules.
concepts.brief: Trace one CUDA source through host compilation and device compilation into virtual and architecture-specific device images inside an executable. Highlight the artifact and diagnostic owned by each stage.
pitfalls: A host executable may contain multiple device images; source text is not the packaged artifact.
PTX and native machine code expose different compilation stages.

headings: `nvcc` packages host code with architecture-specific device images

concepts.title: Distributed object reference
concepts.meaning: A future-like handle connects a remote task result to a consumer while ownership and stored bytes have separate lifetimes.
concepts.brief: Submit several remote feature tasks and keep their ObjectRef handles at the driver. Pass top-level references directly to an actor consumer so the driver need not fetch each payload; reveal local object-store copies, reference counting, owner and reconstructable task lineage as separate layers. Contrast this with serial ray.get submission and an unbounded gather.
pitfalls: An ObjectRef is a handle and dependency, not a location or a guarantee that bytes are resident on one node.
Reference metadata and retained objects still consume resources.
Task-result lineage, actor process state and durable checkpointing are different recovery contracts.

headings: Three pieces of a running job

concepts.title: From token stream to GPT checkpoint
concepts.meaning: A causal decoder predicts the next token, updates weights from loss and samples from the checkpoint.
concepts.brief: Pack a contiguous token stream into context windows and shifted next-token labels. Reveal causal attention, loss and weight update, then sample from the resulting checkpoint and resume from saved optimizer state.
pitfalls: Input tokens and next-token labels are shifted by one position.
Held-out chunks must not be concatenated into fake transitions.

headings: What a resume file has to remember

concepts.title: Grouped GEMM padding and scale
concepts.meaning: Uneven expert token groups pack into an aligned M axis whose padding trades useful work for scheduling efficiency.
concepts.brief: Route tokens into four expert groups with 64, 192, 32 and 128 valid rows. Pack each segment to a declared M alignment, show the concatenated launch grid, highlight useful versus padded rows, and unpack outputs back to original token order. Compare one persistent grouped launch with separate per-expert launches while measuring total time and useful-token throughput.
pitfalls: M counts token-expert assignments, not unique source tokens.
Padding can raise traffic and arithmetic work; a single launch can still win if it amortizes launch cost.
Configured and theoretical alignment helpers may differ on a pinned hardware/library snapshot.

concepts.title: JAX function transformations
concepts.meaning: JAX wraps a pure function with gradient, batching and compilation transformations over pytree state.
concepts.brief: Start with a pure scalar loss over structured parameter leaves. Derive gradients, batch the function with vmap, and compile a shape-specific call with jit, making each transformation visible as a callable wrapper.
pitfalls: Transformations derive callable functions; they are not sequential runtime lifecycle stages.
JIT specialization depends on compatible shapes and static control flow.

headings: Transform one small function at a time
Transformation order changes the derived program

concepts.title: Inspector-executor plan contract
concepts.meaning: A metadata plan assigns irregular requests to GPU tiles and workspace that a stable attention run consumes.
concepts.brief: Show three requests with different query lengths and scattered KV pages. A CPU-side inspector reads offsets and page metadata once, assigns tiles, sizes scratch workspace and decides whether to split KV work. The executor consumes the plan plus query/cache tensors, emits partial states when needed, then merges them. Animate compatibility checks for lengths, masks, pointer layout and workspace lifetime; distinguish a reusable plan from stale decode metadata.
pitfalls: A plan is reusable only across compatible batch specifications; decode lengths can change between steps.
Stable buffer addresses do not make stale metadata contents correct.
The pinned prefill plan performs host-side work and copies, so verify graph-capture constraints for the selected wrapper.

headings: Plan then run: inspector-executor for GPU kernels

concepts.title: Server-side LLM API request
concepts.meaning: An authenticated server turns a user task into a bounded provider request and records the result.
concepts.brief: Route a browser task through backend authentication, tenant authorization, trusted database facts, redaction and a typed provider request. Return a traceable result and show a retry reusing its idempotency key.
pitfalls: Provider credentials stay on the server and outside client bundles.
A timeout leaves the remote outcome uncertain; use idempotency and reconcile before repeating side effects.

headings: A task contract for the model

concepts.title: Runtime buffer lifetime
concepts.meaning: A copy-stream event orders a consumer stream, and the buffer remains alive through consumption and completion.
concepts.brief: Queue a copy on a producer stream, record a ready event and enqueue a consumer wait on another stream. Keep the allocation live through the consumer and release it only after dependent work completes.
pitfalls: A stream wait orders device work without blocking the host.
A wait on an unrecorded event represents empty prior work; record before waiting.

concepts.title: From text to a useful prediction
concepts.meaning: An application collects input, calls a learned model, presents the prediction, and saves useful results.
concepts.brief: Follow one support message from a browser through an HTTP endpoint into a text classifier. Show the returned probability vector, the threshold that selects automatic handling or review, and the saved result. Keep model prediction separate from the routing decision.
pitfalls: A high model score needs measured calibration before it can be read as an observed success rate.
Application tests and labeled model evaluation answer different questions.

headings: Turn that prediction into an API
